description: #3079 — delete_property with a reserved column-backed key (todo_state) clears the block's dedicated column (routed through reserved_key_blocks_column), not a block_properties row. A todo_state is set then deleted; the column ends up null and block_properties stays empty. #3966 — S3 gets a todo_state that is NEVER deleted, and it is what makes this fixture assert anything. Until it was seeded the op list was a pure ROUND TRIP on S2 alone: set todo_state, delete todo_state, ending byte-identical to the seed, so the recorded `expected` was the snapshot the seed alone produces and a mock whose set_todo_state AND delete_property were both no-ops reproduced it exactly. The snapshot-leg vacuity guard in conformance.test.ts caught it. With S3 the terminal state (S2 null, S3 DONE) is reachable only if the set ran and the delete was scoped to the block it named: a no-op set leaves S3 null, a no-op delete leaves S2 TODO, and an over-broad delete clears S3 — all three redden.
name: delete_property_reserved_key_clears_column
